subject: Using filter with position number of variables in dplyr

messages.author: e83d54ec65b5b8e6
messages.subject: Using filter with position number of variables in dplyr
parts:
In dplyr, I can do

mydata %>% select(2:4)

to select the second to fourth variable in a data frame.

Is there an idiom which would allow me to use filter with variable position numbers instead of variable names?

filter(4==1)

does not work, and neither does

filter(`4`==1)

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Using filter with position number of variables in dplyr

messages.subject: Re: Using filter with position number of variables in dplyr
parts:
This works:

filter(mtcars, mtcars[[8]] == 1)

I thought the following might also work in 0.7:

> filter(mtcars, .data[[8]] == 1)
Error in filter_impl(.data, quo) : 
  Evaluation error: Must subset with a string.

This does work but probably doesn't help OP:

filter(mtcars, .data[["vs"]] == 1)
